div.div: Four representative routes to agent memory
How different systems store, revise, and carry state across turns. Representative routes only, based on public documentation and source-available evidence.

div.p: A general memory layer behind many agent stacks.
Extract candidates, retrieve old memories, and decide how to handle them. V2 uses ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NONE; V3 shifts toward ADD-only writing and later consolidation.
Open, configurable, cross-model, and organized by user / session / agent.
Contradictions may coexist until later consolidation.

div.div: Mini-flowNew interaction → extract candidates → retrieve old memory → decide action → write → recall later

div.p: A memory capability inside a domestic open-source RAG + agent platform.
Save message → asynchronous extraction → typed memories → size limit and FIFO forgetting → similarity retrieval.
Platformized, transparent, explicitly typed, with a clear forgetting policy.
Revision is append-oriented; no explicit UPDATE / MERGE loop is exposed.

div.div: Mini-flowAgent message → async extraction → typed store → FIFO management → retrieval → inject

div.p: An open-source agent framework that makes memory a pluggable backend.
Read current MEMORY.md or backend with new dialogue → update via backend or model editing → inject on the next turn.
Pluggable and inspectable; memory can remain human-readable and auditable.
Quality depends on the selected backend or model self-editing.

div.div: Mini-flowDialogue + memory → backend/model update → MEMORY.md or store → inject next turn

div.p: Dify / Coze / FastGPT-style memory assembled through workflow tools.
User input → developer workflow → summary or variables → optional storage → retrieve → prompt injection.
Easy to ship, controllable, and compatible with mature knowledge-base workflows.
Human-written workflow logic decides what is remembered, revised, or forgotten.

div.div: Mini-flowUser input → workflow rules → summary/variables → optional store → retrieve → inject

aside.div: System-led routes decide what to keep and how to revise it.
Workflow-led routes mainly execute developer-written rules.
The question is not whether something is stored, but who decides what survives into the next step.

div.div: Memory is not just persistence. The deeper question is whether a system can revise state and let it shape the next move.
